title: The "Hope is Not a Strategy" Advisory Migration
pattern: Releasing a successor service or API and marking the predecessor as deprecated, but setting no decommissioning deadline or automated migration path.
why_bad: Users will default to the familiar obsolete code. Without a hard deadline, teams prioritize features over migrations, forcing the organization to maintain "dual-system purgatory" indefinitely and doubling operational costs [292, 721, 723].
detection: A deprecated function or service with no corresponding documentation specifying a concrete turndown date, or lacking scheduled "scream tests" (temporary planned outages) to find unknown dependencies [297, 727].
counterexample: Valid for public-facing SDKs where backward compatibility is promised indefinitely to retain user goodwill [738]. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix: Transform the deprecation into a compulsory model: announce a strict decommissioning date, schedule planned outages to expose silent dependencies, and actively run automated migrations [297, 724, 725].
source: Software Engineering at Google, Chapter 15, "Types of Deprecation - Advisory Deprecation" [292, 297, 721, 723, 727]
